summary: beaver-ui-drawer ships install-time and require-time dropper fetching obfuscated remote binary
details: Package published as a UI drawer component contains a postinstall dropper. package.json's postinstall runs setup.js, and index.js (declared main) unconditionally `require('./setup')` inside a try/catch, so both `npm install` and any `require('beaver-ui-drawer')` trigger the same chain. setup.js reconstructs a set of Cloudflare Workers hostnames from split-string arrays (oob-worker.cf99-9b3.workers.dev, cf100-416, cf101-adf, cf102-baf, cf103-070.workers.dev), downloads a platform-specific executable via https.get, and falls back to a covert DNS-TXT channel under *.dl.well1.site (base64-encoded payload assembled from numeric subdomains c.<domain>/<i>.<domain>). The downloaded bytes are written to /tmp or %TEMP% under disguised names (dotnet_diag_<hex>.exe,.cache_<hex>), chmod 0755, and launched detached via execFile with no hash or signature verification. On Windows the code also invokes execSync('powershell...'). The package name and stated purpose (UI drawer library) do not require binary downloads, native execution, or PowerShell invocation, and the destinations are anonymous, obfuscated, and unrelated to any publisher-owned domain.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
